reviewed_by: Claude review of changing model and reasoning effort while a response runs
reason: The chat's Model, Provider and Effort pickers were disabled for the whole of an active response and Core refused both changes then, so a running goal (always mid-response) could never change its model or effort. Core now accepts an effort-only session update and a runtime switch while a turn is active; the switch is saved on the conversation through a new apply endpoint after the existing preflight and compaction confirmation; settling a turn keeps the conversation's newer runtime and settings instead of writing the turn's back; goal continuations and queued provider follow-ups read the conversation's current model and effort; a follow-up whose conversation changed provider is routed to review; harness follow-ups may carry a newly picked model. The selected Python files cover the runtime switch and compaction gate (test_chat), the API guard and new endpoint (test_chat_api), goal continuation across a mid-turn switch (test_chat_goals), queue adoption, provider review and harness model follow-ups (test_chat_queue), and schedules, which follow the conversation's runtime (test_chat_schedules). The client unit tests cover the new apply call and the effort-only save. Playwright selects the provider runtime switch area (the confirmed and verified switches now save on the conversation, plus a new mid-response test that also exercises the stale-revision retry), the provider reasoning area that drives the effort picker, and the real-Core goal lifecycle entry, which now changes the effort during a live goal turn and checks the stop does not overwrite it.
exclusions: Full Python, frontend and Playwright suites are excluded. Harness runtime code is unchanged; the harness follow-up path is covered by the queue test that drives a real harness turn with a new model. No native tests are selected because no Rust changed. The broad assistant Playwright area is excluded because the only controls whose behaviour changed are the assistant settings pickers, which the selected areas render on desktop and both phone projects.
